items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: I hear a lot of people talking about him, but Al Wynn, is he from New Orleans?

ctx.x: Was he a real tonk trombone player? I was? Tonk trombone player, could he play dirty? I didn't, I didn't know him to play like dirty. I know he played the music and stuff. Yeah. He could really beat a bass. He did.

Mm-hmm. One fellow I wanna ask you, maybe you don't know, but the seems that I never asked him, it seems like he's from here, but I hear a lot of people talking about him, but Al Wynn, is he from New Orleans? Yeah?

Yeah, but I don't think he played down here. We were talking about that, Willie Humphrey was saying how many guys were from here like Simeon and Al Wynn and they didn't play anything down here. Uh-huh. Preston Jackson, you know.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: I made records with me and Al Wynn

ctx.x: He was on, he might have played bass on some of them records I made, I don't know, because I was with him right now. But I'll tell you the band, I made records with me and Al Wynn, then I made records with Francois Luzan, I made records with Jimmy Weed, I made records with Tiny Palm, then I made some of my own, you know, with a bunch I had. Somebody else I made records with, I can't think, no. I made records with a lot of guys.
I was just thinking about Tiny Palm, did you ever play any of his arrangements?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: Francois was on the drums. And we had Al Wins a lot of different times.

ctx.x: Who was in the band ready to go to the world?

Well, a fellow on guitar named Charles Ducasten. A big stout fellow played clarinet and saxophone named Fred Howard. And Fred Reeves on the piano. I was on the trumpet. Francois was on the drums. And we had Al Wins a lot of different times. Now, I'll tell you who worked with us there a long time. People would not believe that, but it's true. You heard of Ted Wilson? Oh, yeah. Well, he worked right there with us a long time after he left his dorm. Oh, no. Did you know that band from Kansas City? A fellow that died…
I don't know anything about that. Ted did.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Well yeah, Al when was doing the hiring, I know that, he hired me.

ctx.x: Where at? At the Dreamland in Chicago. That's your first job on then?

Well yeah, I had a first job I went on in Chicago outside of the Miramac Miramaker show. Yeah. We was working at the Monogram Theater, but I was Dublin. I would leave there and go into the Dreamland right across the street, see, and play there with them. Yeah. So it sort of had two leaders in, really, huh? Well yeah, Al when was doing the hiring, I know that, he hired me. Mm-hmm. But Tiny Palm was writing all the music and taking everything else. How big a band was that? Well then they had something like twelve…

Was that when you made the recordings with Palm? Yeah, yeah, same time. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. So, uh, you might have had some of the same men on the Palm records that you had on the Al Wynn records. That's a possibility.
